what: Behind the panel, one WebGL2 layer lays 2px dots on every 30px cell (on tall screens the cells shrink by the height/width ratio). .3s after opening, a diagonal wave (width .2) passes from bottom left to top right over 1.7s with power3.out and the dots rise — the dots are briefly larger at the wave’s tail. Only while the mouse moves, the dots around it (20% of the panel width) are pushed away like a lens (−300) and the radius grows up to 6.4% of the cell. The cursor position follows slowly with 1−e^(−.004·dt), and the response is only the per-frame travel distance (px), cooled by the same factor, speed × .075, so it settles back in place when the mouse stops

options.min: Dot size (cell ratio, diameter share), default .07
options.max: Max growth around the cursor, default .4
options.push: Push strength (device pixels), default −300 — negative pushes outward and bulges
options.reveal: Diagonal reveal duration (sec), default 1.7 — 0 means immediate

note: The original shader was not ported, it was rewritten with the same values (cells 30 · dots .07/.4 · push −300 · radius .2 · speed ×.15/2 · wave .2 · 1.7s power3.out). On touch devices (hover false) cursor response is off as in the original and only the reveal plays. Drawing pauses once the cursor stops and the reveal ends

from.where: index.html .ct-grid (screen-fixed background, transparent .3, dots #bcbcbc) — original BaseGrid (CELL_SIZE 30 · uDotMinSize .07 · uDotMaxSize .4 · uRepulseStrength −300 · uRepulseSize .2 · reveal 1.7s power3.out debounce 300ms)
